subject.title: feat(crestodian): AI-only conversation with model-judged approvals

question: After the command-pivot regression is fixed and real behavior proof is added, should Crestodian accept model-judged approval intent for state-changing operations in this PR?
rationale: The patch addresses a real setup/security bug, but approval intent classification and immediate host directives are a product and security boundary that should not be accepted solely by automation.

options.title: Fix and proceed with guarded approval intent
options.body: Repair the command-pivot bug, add proof, and let a maintainer review the final model-judged approval semantics before merge.

options.title: Narrow to deterministic approval first
options.body: Keep the anchored command and redaction fixes but defer model-judged approval intent to a smaller follow-up decision.

options.title: Split the broad change
options.body: Close or pause this branch and land narrower PRs for parser safety, approval behavior, directives, redaction, and Gemini parity separately.

recommendation.title: Fix and proceed with guarded approval intent
recommendation.body: Repair the command-pivot bug, add proof, and let a maintainer review the final model-judged approval semantics before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Crestodian feature history and the linked issue both point to `steipete` as the best product/security-boundary owner for this decision.
